Name: Pre-diagnosis
Description: - Patient goes for tests, and mammogragm , Ultasound, US and biopsy. It can be either of the following- Mammogram + Biopsy, or US + bioposy or MMG+US_Biopsy

Name: Results Clinic
Description: Patient is given diagnosis for the first time. This is a very sensitive step as the patient is hearing the news for the first time

Transition notes from this stage to next: further investigations needed before treatment decision

Name: palliative
Description: Metastasis has happened and hence curative treatment is not possible.

Name: primary endocrine
Description:
endocrine (anti hormone medication) as first line treatment . 
There are multiple reasons for chosing this treatment path, the most common one being patient may not be fit for surgery.
Transition notes from this stage to next: Hormone therapy is effective on the patient
If Horome therapy is not working, we directly go to surgery

Name: Follow-up Clinic
Description: follow up to see if hormone treatment is working with a Specialist Clinician (this is not same as results clinic)

Name: Continue same endocrine treatment
Description: If, on follow up, cancer is reducing in size, then you are okay to continue on same medication

Name: Change to another medication
Description: If, on follow up, cancer is getting bigger, then doctors will put you on another anti hormone medication, or discuss surgery with you (see stage 2)

Name: Further investigation
Description: Following review of previous work up in the MDM, patient is reviewed in results clinic  to discuss next step, which could be either to start treatment or for further investigation,

Name: Surgery
Description: Master Stage for various surgery types. The patient may go through some of the surgies in the steps 2.1 or 2.2 etc. and end up in a psot surgery MDM where the next stpes are defined.

Name: Breast surgery
Description: Operations on the breast to remove cancer and, when possible, preserve appearance and function

Name: Breast Conservation Surgery
Description: Operations which remove the cancer while keeping most of the breast, almost always followed by radiotherapy

Name: Wide local excision
Description: Operation to removes the cancer with a margin of healthy tissue, keeping the rest of the breast, when the cancer to breast size ratio allows (for example, small cancer in large breast)

Name: Oncoplastic Breast Conservation Surgery
Description: Operations which combines cancer removal with plastic surgery techniques to improve breast shap.

Name: Therapeutic mammaplasty/mammoplasty
Description: Operation which  combines cancer removal, with breast-reduction techniques, allowing removal of bigger cancer from big/droopy breast. This may or may not be comined with reduction of the other breast to symmetrize

Name: Chest wall perforator flap
Description: Operation which  combines cancer removal, and use of nearby skin and fat to fill the defect after cancer removal,  allowing removal of bigger cancer from small breast

Name: Mastectomy
Description: Operations which remove all the breast tissue, including the cancer

Name: Simple mastectomy no reconstruction
Description: Operation which remove all the breast tissue, including the cancer without rebuilding (going flat chest, with scar)

Name: Mastectomy and reconstruction
Description: Operation which remove all the breast tissue, including the cancer,  and rebuild the breast mound

Name: autologous reconstruction
Description: Breast rebuilt using your own tissue from another body area

Name: Implant based reconstruction
Description: Breast rebuilt using a silicone or saline implant

Name: Axillary surgery
Description: Surgery to assess or treat lymph nodes under the arm, helping guide breast cancer treatment decisions.

Name: No surgery
Description: No indication to remove or sample lymph nodes under the arm, because the risk of cancer spread is very low, usally in case of (non invasive breast cancer)

Name: Sentinel lymph node biopsy
Description: Operation in which only the first 1-3 draining lymph nodes are removed  to check for cancer spread.

Name: Axillary Lymph node clearance
Description: Operation in which "all" underarm lymph nodes are removed to treat  known cancer spread, and assess cancer burden to plan further treatments.This is done when there is confimed cancer spread in the lymph nodes.

Name:
Neoadjuvant 
systemic 
treatment
Description: Treatment given before surgery to shrink the cancer and improve surgical and long-term outcomes.

Name: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy
Description: Anti-cancer drugs given before surgery to kill cancer cells

Name: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy with immunotherapy
Description: Chemotherapy combined with immune-boosting treatment, before surgery, to help your body attack cancer cells, usually used in specifc breast cancer type (called triple negative cancer)

Name: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy with targeted therapy
Description: Chemotherapy combined with drugs targeting specific cancer features or pathways, before surgery, improving response to chemotherapy, and and reducing recurrence risk, usually used in specifc breast cancer type (e.g. blocking growth factor receptors in HER2 +ve cancer)

Name: Neoadjuvant endocrine treatment
Description: Hormone-blocking treatment, given before surgery, to slow growth of cancer if you are temporary unfit for surgery, or to shrink the cancer if you are unfit for traditional chemotherapy. This can be only used in hormone-sensitive breast cancer,

Name: Further surgery
Description: After pathology review of the first surgery, further surgery may be needed if there is suspicion of residual cancer in the breast or in the lymph nodes

Name: Axilla lymph node clearance
Description: Operation in which "all" underarm lymph nodes are removed to treat  known cancer spread, and assess cancer burden to plan further treatments.This is done when there is confimed cancer spread in the lymph nodes.

Name: Breast margin excision
Description: operation in which breast  tissue (suspected to contain residual cancer), is removed.

Name: Further breast margin excision
Description: operation in which further tissue (suspected to contain residual cancer), is removed from the breast

Name: Completion mastectomy
Description: operation in which all breast tissue is removed, as it is suscpected to contain residual cancer

Name: No further surgery
Description: No need for further operation, as there residual cancer is not suspected

Name: No adjuvant treatment
Description: No need for further treatment after surgery

Name: Adjuvant treatment
Description: Further treatment is needed after surgery, aiming mainly to reduce risk of recurrence

Name: Adjuvant radiotherapy
Description: Treament with radiation to the breast (after breast conservation surgery), or to chest wall (after mastecomy, advanced cancer), or to other nodal areas (like supraclavicular or internal mammary areas)

Name: adjuvant chemotherapy
Description: Systemic adminstration of medications to kill cancer cells. Chemotherapy may be combined with immunotherapy (for triple negative cancer), or targeted therapy (in HER2 positive cancer), or with zoledronic acid (for women with high risk breast cancer, to reduce risk of bone recurrence)

Name: No adjuvant  endocrine therapy
Description: endocrine therapy not indciated in patient with non hormonally sensitive breast cancer

Name: adjuvant  endocrine therapy only
Description: endocrine therapy is indciated in patients with estrogen receptor positive breast cancer

Name: adjuvant  endocrine therap, and zoledronic acid
Description: In postmenopasual women, zoledronic acid is indicated, in combination with endocrine therapy, to improve survival by inhibiting bone breakdown
